message: Review complete: 1 finding(s) across 3 selected item(s).

comments.content: `--ignore-failed-read` does not cover the mid-write scenario the comment claims it tolerates. It only suppresses failures on files tar cannot *open* (vanished between walk and read). A file that *changes while being read* — e.g. an active turn appending to a `.workflow-data` file while tar reads it — still makes GNU tar emit "file changed as we read it" and **exit with status 1**. Under `set -euo pipefail` (line 9) the script aborts right here: the retention pruning (bounded at KEEP=14) and the `tar -tzf` integrity gate never run, and the cron job reports failure. Concrete failure: nightly 03:17 run overlaps a running turn writing events → tar exit 1 → script dies mid-run; archives then accumulate unpruned on /data since retention is skipped on every such run. Exit code 1 means "warnings only" (archive still valid best-effort snapshot, per the header's stated semantics); only 2 is fatal — tolerate 1 explicitly.
comments.suggestion_code:
tar_rc=0
tar -czf "$DEST/factory-data-$stamp.tar.gz" \
  --ignore-failed-read \
  -C "$REPO/.eve" .workflow-data blob-data 2>/dev/null || tar_rc=$?
# GNU tar: 0 = clean, 1 = warnings only (e.g. "file changed as we read it" while a
# turn appends live), 2 = fatal. 1 is acceptable best-effort snapshot semantics.
[ "$tar_rc" -le 1 ] || exit "$tar_rc"

**agent/sandbox/Dockerfile** — curl + ca-certificates are installed in the earlier layer (line 10), so the new RUN works. Keyring pattern (armored .asc + signed-by) is valid on Debian bookworm/trixie base. `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` matches existing style. No issue. (arch=amd64 restriction: build already proven on host per background; not a defect.)

**scripts/backup-factory-data.sh** — one real issue: `--ignore-failed-read` only covers files tar cannot open (vanished between walk and read). It does NOT cover the "file changed as we read it" case — when a turn appends to a workflow-data file while tar is mid-read, GNU tar emits that warning and **exits 1**. Under `set -euo pipefail`, that aborts the script: retention pruning and the integrity gate are skipped and the cron run fails — exactly the live-write scenario the header comment says the script tolerates. Repeated overlapping runs also mean retention never executes, so archives accumulate beyond KEEP on /data.

Fix: tolerate exit 1 explicitly (1 = warnings, 2 = fatal).
